Below we establish a simple"}, {"line": 112, "text": "mapping against the ``my_data`` table::"}, {"line": 113, "text": ""}, {"line": 114, "text": "    from sqlalchemy import mapper"}, {"line": 115, "text": ""}, {"line": 116, "text": "    class MyDataClass(object):"}, {"line": 117, "text": "        pass"}, {"line": 118, "text": ""}, {"line": 119, "text": "    # associates mutation listeners with MyDataClass.data"}, {"line": 120, "text": "    mapper(MyDataClass, my_data)"}, {"line": 121, "text": ""}, {"line": 122, "text": "The ``MyDataClass.data`` member will now be notified of in place changes"}, {"line": 123, "text": "to its value."}, {"line": 124, "text": ""}, {"line": 125, "text": "There's no difference in usage when using declarative::"}, {"line": 126, "text": ""}, {"line": 127, "text": "    from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base"}, {"line": 128, "text": ""}, {"line": 129, "text": "    Base = declarative_base()"}, {"line": 130, "text": ""}, {"line": 131, "text": "    class MyDataClass(Base):"}, {"line": 132, "text": "        __tablename__ = 'my_data'"}, {"line": 133, "text": "        id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)"}, {"line": 134, "text": "        data = Column(MutableDict.as_mutable(JSONEncodedDict))"}, {"line": 135, "text": ""}, {"line": 136, "text": "Any in-place changes to the ``MyDataClass.data`` member"}, {"line": 137, "text": "will flag the attribute as \"dirty\" on the parent object::"}, {"line": 138, "text": ""}, {"line": 139, "text": "    >>> from sqlalchemy.orm import Session"}, {"line": 140, "text": ""}, {"line": 141, "text": "    >>> sess = Session()"}, {"line": 142, "text": "    >>> m1 = MyDataClass(data={'value1':'foo'})"}, {"line": 143, "text": "    >>> sess.add(m1)"}, {"line": 144, "text": "    >>> sess.commit()"}, {"line": 145, "text": ""}, {"line": 146, "text": "    >>> m1.data['value1'] = 'bar'"}, {"line": 147, "text": "    >>> assert m1 in sess.dirty"}, {"line": 148, "text": "    True"}, {"line": 149, "text": ""}, {"line": 150, "text": "The ``MutableDict`` can be associated with all future instances"}, {"line": 151, "text": "of ``JSONEncodedDict`` in one step, using"}, {"line": 152, "text": ":meth:`~.Mutable.associate_with`. In our case, this is a good thing, since if this dictionary were"}, {"line": 174, "text": "picklable, it could lead to an excessively large pickle size for our value"}, {"line": 175, "text": "objects that are pickled by themselves outside of the context of the parent."}, {"line": 176, "text": "The developer responsibility here is only to provide a ``__getstate__`` method"}, {"line": 177, "text": "that excludes the :meth:`~MutableBase._parents` collection from the pickle"}, {"line": 178, "text": "stream::"}, {"line": 179, "text": ""}, {"line": 180, "text": "    class MyMutableType(Mutable):"}, {"line": 181, "text": "        def __getstate__(self):"}, {"line": 182, "text": "            d = self.__dict__.copy()"}, {"line": 183, "text": "            d.pop('_parents', None)"}, {"line": 184, "text": "            return d"}, {"line": 185, "text": ""}, {"line": 186, "text": "With our dictionary example, we need to return the contents of the dict itself"}, {"line": 187, "text": "(and also restore them on __setstate__)::"}, {"line": 188, "text": ""}, {"line": 189, "text": "    class MutableDict(Mutable, dict):"}, {"line": 190, "text": "        # ...."}, {"line": 191, "text": ""}, {"line": 192, "text": "        def __getstate__(self):"}, {"line": 193, "text": "            return dict(self)"}, {"line": 194, "text": ""}, {"line": 195, "text": "        def __setstate__(self, state):"}, {"line": 196, "text": "            self.update(state)"}, {"line": 197, "text": ""}, {"line": 198, "text": "In the case that our mutable value object is pickled as it is attached to one"}, {"line": 199, "text": "or more parent objects that are also part of the pickle, the :class:`.Mutable`"}, {"line": 200, "text": "mixin will re-establish the :attr:`.Mutable._parents` collection on each value"}], "source_version": "b1421c9fd59154e063ac0d0a98dd2370cdb225043de93162d8691361fca728b2"}

function.name: apply_edits
function.description: Atomically replace inclusive 1-based line spans. Every source_version must equal the current file hash returned by read_source. All spans in one file refer to the same original version and must not overlap. new is the full replacement text, including needed newlines. Use start_line=end_line=0 and source_version="new" only to create an absent authorized file. Only task-authorized source and tests/test_regression.py may change; all changed Python files must parse.
